cultural.vision_reason: The picture shows a pair of traditional decorated leather riding boots, plausibly Hausa footwear from Niger, so it fits the claimed ethnicity and garment category.

physical.title: boot
physical.summary: Pair of man's yellow-dyed leather riding boots. Boots are cut diagonally at the top and oversewn with red wool thread on one side and natural-coloured silk thread on the other. Front of each boot has red, white and blue silk thread pompom. Boot legs decorated with punched circles and incised lines; one side of each boot has circle of yellow-dyed leather sewn on and decorated with eight-pointed star in red, green and blue cotton thread. Further decorated with five hemispherical metal studs and concentric circles sewn in lines of green, blue and red cotton thread. Leather circle has alternating blue and white cotton edging. Strip of green-dyed leather between boot legs and uppers. Soles of red-dyed goat skin. All seams are hand sewn using cotton thread.

physical.title: tunic
physical.summary: Child's bolero composed of hand plain woven cotton: dyed red blue and bleached white warps and dyed black blue and bleached white wefts. This combination of warps and wefts this creates red warp stripes at regular intervals crossed by pairs of black weft stripes at regular intervals on a light blue background. The front of the bolero is heavily embroidered with geometric patterns in dyed red, green, black, red and blue wool. There are also a number of tassels in dyed red and green wool attached. The back of bolero has a single panel of dyed red wool supplementary weft work. There are also sixteen areas of tassels created using supplementary weft work in dyed red and blue cotton. The sleeves and base of the garment are edges with dyed orange synthetic material.

cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a traditional indigo-and-white Hausa men’s gown (tobe/boubou) with handwoven checked cloth and embroidered decoration, fitting the claimed Hausa ethnicity and garment category.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe, riga) of hand-spun white and indigo cotton. The body is formed of 56 narrow strips hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally. The body of the gown is rectangular in shape, while the sleeves are wider at the top than the bottom and therefore fan out along the top. A large pocket is sewn onto the front. All the strips have the same design of indigo cotton crossed in both warp and weft by lines of white cotton that form a narrow check (etu). The front of the cloth is embroidered by hand in white European cotton in the ‘eight knives’ (aska takwas) pattern. The areas showing the knives are embroidered on other pieces of cloth, which were then couched down; the rest of the decoration is embroidered directly on the strips in chain and buttonhole eyelet stitching, with knots, spirals and other interlaced patterns; there is also a second small spiral on the back. The gown is unlined, and has been hemmed around the neck and sleeves.

physical.title: shirt; tobe
physical.summary: Boy’s gown or boubou (Af1966,01.2b are the matching trousers), made of imported European cotton sheeting, which has been tailored to shape and assembled using a sewing machine. The cotton has been decorated by sewing over the surface a white cotton thread to imitate a damask weave and the pattern formed by lengths of strip-weave sewn together. Two large decorative panels of circles and knots are sewn in yellow imported thread on the front and back, with extensive use of buttonhole eyelet stitching.

physical.title: skirt
physical.summary: Woman's skirt: composed of four pieces of machine plain woven cotton sections. there are two large sections of imitation Adire decorated cotton machine sewn together to make the body of the skirt with a long piece of natural coloured cotton sewn along the top to act as ties. The body of the skirt has been starch resist dyed forming rows of combs and invertebrates separated by blocks of stripes. There is a pocket imitating the pockets found on male gowns (i.e. Af1934, 0307. 206). The pocket has been extensively machine embroidered in dyed red and yellow cotton and bleached white cotton. The pocket is lined with a piece of buff coloured cotton (calico).
